result.summary: The intersection features high-visibility zebra crosswalks and vehicle traffic signals, providing basic infrastructure for pedestrians. However, the lack of dedicated pedestrian signal heads and the presence of sidewalk gaps on certain corners reduce overall safety and accessibility.

hazards.name: Missing Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: There are no dedicated walk/don't-walk signals, forcing pedestrians to interpret vehicle signals which may not account for all turning movements.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Discontinuity
hazards.description: The sidewalk terminates into a grassy area on the far right corner, creating an inaccessible path for those with mobility aids and forcing pedestrians into the roadway.
hazards.location_in_image: Far right corner of the intersection

interventions.title: Install Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Add dedicated pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to all corners to provide clear crossing intervals.

interventions.title: Complete Sidewalk Network
interventions.description: Construct paved sidewalks where gaps currently exist to ensure a continuous and accessible pedestrian route.

result.summary: The intersection lacks fundamental pedestrian infrastructure, including sidewalks, marked crosswalks, and pedestrian signals. While vehicle traffic is controlled by signals, the environment is hostile for pedestrians who must navigate unpaved grass or the roadway.

hazards.name: Missing Sidewalks
hazards.description: There are no paved walkways for pedestrians, forcing them to walk on grass or in the roadway.

hazards.name: Unmarked Crossing
hazards.description: Despite being a signalized intersection, there are no marked crosswalks to guide pedestrians or alert drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Across all legs of the intersection

hazards.name: Lack of Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: No pedestrian-specific signal heads are visible, leaving pedestrians to rely on vehicle signals which may not provide adequate clearance time.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Installation
interventions.description: Construct ADA-compliant sidewalks on both sides of the street to provide a dedicated space for pedestrians.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalks
interventions.description: Paint continental or ladder-style crosswalks to clearly define pedestrian paths and increase driver awareness.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Signal Heads
interventions.description: Install countdown pedestrian signals to provide clear information on when it is safe to cross.

result.summary: The intersection features a marked crosswalk and a sidewalk, providing basic pedestrian infrastructure. However, safety is compromised by significant visual obstructions from dense vegetation at the corner and a lack of visible traffic control devices for the roadway.

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: Dense vegetation at the corner significantly blocks sightlines between pedestrians at the crosswalk and approaching drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: The corner area between the two intersecting roads.

hazards.name: Uncontrolled Crossing
hazards.description: The marked crosswalk lacks active traffic control like stop signs or signals, relying solely on driver yielding behavior.
hazards.location_in_image: The roadway at the marked crosswalk.

interventions.title: Vegetation Management
interventions.description: Trim or remove the dense trees and bushes at the corner to restore clear sightlines for all road users.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions to shorten the pedestrian crossing distance and improve the visibility of pedestrians to drivers.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk Markings
interventions.description: Replace the standard transverse lines with high-visibility ladder or zebra markings to increase the conspicuity of the crossing.

result.summary: The intersection is equipped with marked zebra crosswalks and overhead traffic signals within a residential context. While basic pedestrian infrastructure like sidewalks and curb ramps are present, the absence of visible dedicated pedestrian signal heads and some pavement degradation are notable deficiencies.

hazards.name: Missing Pedestrian Signals
hazards.description: No dedicated pedestrian signal heads are visible at the intersection, requiring pedestrians to rely on vehicular signals which may not provide sufficient clearance intervals.

hazards.name: Pavement Cracking
hazards.description: Visible cracks and surface degradation in the roadway and crosswalk area could pose a tripping hazard or impede users with mobility devices.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Signal Installation
interventions.description: Install dedicated pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to provide clear right-of-way and timing information for people crossing.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Implement bulb-outs at the corners to shorten the crossing distance and reduce the speed of turning vehicles.

interventions.title: Pavement Resurfacing
interventions.description: Repair and resurface the intersection to provide a smooth, hazard-free path for pedestrians and cyclists.
